Text: The resultant displacement is {{c1::the vector sum of the individual displacements}}.
Back Extra:
Ex: "In other words, the resultant displacement vector has a magnitude of 11.2 km and makes an angle θ = 27° with the positive x axis."

Distinguish: the resultant's magnitude is smaller than the plain sum of the leg lengths unless the legs point the same way — walking 10.0 km east then 5.0 km north gives an 11.2 km resultant, while 15 km is the distance traveled.

Cue: add the vectors tail-to-tip; the resultant is the arrow drawn from the tail of the first vector to the tip of the second.
